allowances: fs.write `claude-code.git-internals`: user settings cannot name the project, so sandboxed commands may write `.git` (objects, refs, index: `git commit` works) in every directory, except what makes git run code or follow another repository (hooks, config, config.worktree, info/attributes, a linked worktree's commondir, the same in submodules); a script can still rewrite history or create a `.git` file (`gitdir: …`) in a subdirectory, and the hook still asks for file-tool writes to any `.git`
fs.read `sandbox.read_roots`: the hook decides these reads by the rules (ask by default); OS layers allow them so commands can run, and deny rules still win

fs.write `claude-code.directory-nodes`: a directory in denyWrite covers its subtree, so these directory nodes are left out and only the files below them are denied; renaming or deleting the directory itself is left to the hook

fs.read `claude-code.system-paths`: Claude Code closes reads only under the user directories (/Users, /home, /Volumes, /media, /root); other paths that are not read roots stay readable for sandboxed commands

fs.write `claude-code.working-directories`: sandboxed commands may write the session's working directories and temp directory; OpenMoat's project is the git root and never the home directory, so a session started above a project writes more than the hook allows
losses: fs.read `secrets-paths`: Claude Code would re-open the exceptions (**/.env.example, **/.env.sample, **/.env.template) outside the working directories too, so they are left out: denied for sandboxed commands

fs.write `secrets-paths`: Claude Code would re-open the exceptions (**/.env.example, **/.env.sample, **/.env.template) outside the working directories too, so they are left out: denied for sandboxed commands
fs.write `project-fs`: user settings cannot name the project, so `.moat/**` is denied in every directory

fs.read `claude-code.static-denies`: Claude Code's own deny rules for these paths hold for its file tools when the hook does not run, and refuse an exception the hook allows (such as `.env.example`) too
fs.read `default`: Claude Code's file tools refuse reads outside the working directories (permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories) where the hook would ask; `/add-dir` adds a directory
